notes: 2026-09-23 fix round, props update() perf — the largest remaining item on the priority list, saved for last as planned (90-175x over the ARCHITECTURE <=1.5ms/frame budget on every preset, critic round 3). Root cause confirmed by reading grass.js directly: a camera jump past the 14m re-pack threshold called rebuild(), which synchronously generated EVERY not-yet-cached chunk in range (up to ~221 chunks x ~1,300-1,600 sample() candidates each) before packing anything — and since a showcase preset switch IS such a threshold crossing, this fired on every single preset load, exactly matching the critic's 'not a rare edge case, the normal cost of a camera jump' framing. Fix: split the old synchronous rebuild() into _queueMissing() (diffs the chunks needed for a new view against the cache, closest-first) + _drainQueue() (generates a time/count-bounded slice per update() call, ~3ms/<=24 chunks) + _repack() (packs whatever is currently cached, silently skipping chunks still queued rather than generating them inline). The field now visibly grows in over a couple of seconds on a big jump instead of freezing for one. Two cases deliberately keep the OLD synchronous-and-complete behaviour, both reasoned through explicitly rather than assumed: the very first population after a fresh load (a one-time loading cost, not the repeated-jump stutter being fixed), and every update while ctx.isShowcase is true (a preset load is a one-shot static render for screenshots/critics, not live gameplay — the tooling needs a fully-populated field on capture, not one mid-stream). Caught and fixed my own mistake mid-verification: my first test script called the wrong CameraRig API (setCamera expects raw {x,y,z,tx,ty,tz}, not {target,distance,pitch,yaw} — that's lookAt/apply) and silently NaN'd the camera position; re-derived the correct call from CameraRig.js itself before re-testing. Verified with a real, direct measurement, not just code inspection: in --game mode (not showcase), a 424m lookAt() jump queued 205 missing chunks and drained them at 6-17ms per frame (grassPendingChunks counted down 205->193 over 8 sampled frames while grassInstances grew 12,184->25,159) instead of one 450+ms synchronous frame — confirmed against a same-session control measurement of the pre-fix code (git stash), which measured 447ms for the identical scenario in this same (heavily loaded, consistently ~10-50x slower than the critic's original environment all session) sandbox, ruling out 'the critic's baseline was measured somewhere faster' as an alternative explanation for the improvement. Showcase mode re-verified fully populated (grassPendingChunks: 0, ~180-194k instances, matching the critic's own measured range) with matching screenshots (props-overview-fix.png, props-grass-fix.png) showing no visual regression. Honest limitation, stated in the module's own README rather than smoothed over: the packing step itself (_repack) is not amortised and its cost grows as more chunks stream in (observed up to ~10ms once several hundred chunks were cached) — per-frame cost during an active big jump is now 6-17ms, a genuine ~10-40x improvement over the measured 132-263ms/447-552ms baseline and no longer a single catastrophic freeze, but not yet hitting the strict 1.5ms target on every streaming frame; flagged as the natural next step rather than claimed as a full budget-compliant fix. Score not touched — pending critic re-verification, per this project's established division of labour.

2026-09-22 fix round, savannah/park camera-anchor systemic issue the critic flagged as shared between the two modules — turned out to be two genuinely different root causes, not one. (1) savannah 'close' preset shared the EXACT same (gx,gz) anchor as 'herd' (aim(presets.close, gx, gz) and aim(presets.herd, gx, gz) both, differentiated only by distance/pitch/yaw), and the herd's own zebra/wildebeest spawn only ~8-14m from that same point and walks through it — so 'quiet foreground grass and an acacia trunk, kopje softening into haze behind' was structurally guaranteed to show the herd crossing instead. Fixed by giving close its own anchor, searched perpendicular to the herd's travel line (candidate offsets at 70/90/110/130m each way, validated against real height/slope/biome via ctx.world) so it lands on genuine open grassland clear of the herd's spawn/walk corridor for any seed, with yaw re-derived via degOf toward the kopje for compositional consistency with the other kopje-facing presets. Verified: savannah-close-fixed2.png shows quiet foreground grass, an acacia trunk, and a hazy ridge behind, no herd in frame. (2) park 'habitat' and 'close' were NOT actually a shared-anchor bug like savannah's — closer investigation (via __SIM__ eval diagnostics reading the actual build report and querying terrain distances directly, not guessing from screenshots alone) found 'habitat' was a genuine BUILD-TIME SITING bug: the plains habitat's own anchor landed 3.2m from the river's edge, in wetland biome (confirmed numerically), for reasons upstream of any camera code — build.js's vertex-openness scoring (min(distToKopjes, distToWater)) can rank a vertex 'open' on kopje-distance alone while still being river-adjacent, and the later offRoad() inward nudge (toward loopCenter, up to 70% of the habitat radius) only had a 30m local search window to rescue that, nowhere near enough when the whole neighbourhood is riverside. Fixed at the actual source in two layers: vertex selection for plains/browsers now prefers a candidate with 55m+ real water clearance before falling back to the old kopje-only rule (build.js's plainsIdx/browsersIdx selection), and offRoad's own rescue search widened from 30m to 60m specifically when avoiding water. Camera-side, 'habitat' now aims 35% of the way from the anchor toward the real hidePlains building position (the vantage a visitor / viewing hide actually has) instead of the disc's dead centre from 110-140m away, with distance cut to 55m and pitch to 14 so the fenced grazers read as the subject instead of a small element in a wide aerial shot. Verified via a real coordinate probe (not just eyeballing): before the build.js fix, camera target was 3.2m from the river; after, park-habitat-final2.png shows open dry plains with acacias, a water pump, fencing and grazing animals, kopje visible in the distance — correct biome, no river. 'close' (the lodge veranda/pool shot) was a straightforward camera bug like the original hypothesis, but needed two attempts to get right: the pool's local-space position (7.5, 14.15 in lodge.js's own coordinate system) is now rotated into world space using the LODGE BUILDING's actual placed rotation (report.buildings.lodge.rot, newly exposed — placeBuilding can offset the real building up to 60m from its site anchor, so lodgeSite was the wrong reference point entirely). First attempt used a yaw sign that put the camera on the building's INTERIOR side, walking it straight through the roof/pool geometry as distance increased (caught via screenshot: an unreadable extreme close-up on straw-roof texture, camera clearly clipped through the mesh) — traced to a sign error against CameraRig.js's own camera-placement formula (target + distance*(sin(yaw),cos(yaw)), verified line-by-line against buildings/index.js's lamp-placement transform to get the rotation convention right) and corrected. Verified: park-close-final.png shows a proper eye-level veranda shot — thatch roof, timber poles, stone plinth, railings and steps all clearly framed. Regression-checked lodge, night, and overview presets after all build.js/showcase.js changes: all clean, no defects introduced. As with every prior fix this round, none of the affected modules' numeric scores were touched — re-scoring is the critic's job, pending re-verification.

2026-09-22 fix round, terrain escarpment 'fluted column' repeating-groove artifact — the critic's most consequential remaining shader/noise item (2 different presets plus an extra angle all showed the same 'every groove near-identical width/spacing... a repeating procedural column motif rather than natural stratified rock'). Root cause: the cliff-face groove noise (generate.js, the escarpment block) fed a FIXED frequency (x/26, x/8.5) straight into ridged noise with no domain warp, which is close to worst-case for producing a uniform comb — ridged noise at one fixed frequency has one dominant wavelength, and integer-multiple octaves reinforce rather than break that regularity. Fixed using the same domain-warping technique the codebase's own noise.warped2D helper already uses for fbm (perturb the sample position with an independent, much-lower-frequency field before evaluating the ridged noise), applied locally in generate.js rather than touching the shared Noise.js class (smaller blast radius — this noise feeds actual heightfield data other systems read, not just a texture). Two independent low-frequency fbm fields (170m and 130m wavelength, decorrelated from each other and from the two ridged fields via distinct coordinate offsets, matching the file's own existing idiom for decorrelating noise channels) warp the x/z fed to each ridged evaluation; a third slow field modulates groove DEPTH (0.6-1.0x) so some flutes read stronger than others along the ridge, per the critic's own suggested fix direction ('stronger domain warp per-groove, vary groove depth along the ridge'). Verified via fresh screenshots at both previously-bad presets (terrain-escarpment-fixed.png, terrain-overview-fixed.png): groove spacing, width and depth now visibly vary along the ridge instead of reading as a uniform repeating comb. Honest caveat: this is a genuine improvement, confirmed by direct comparison, but I have not attempted to quantify 'irregular enough' the way the roads swirl fix was eventually pixel-diff-verified — worth the critic's own fresh eyes on whether residual regularity remains at very close range.

2026-09-22 fix round, roads asphalt swirl — the hardest item in this round by far, worth documenting the method since the obvious fix didn't work. Critic finding: 'swirled/brushed pattern... more like sand-blasted concrete than fine, uniform pebble-speckle'. First attempt (raise the aggregate noise's octaves/frequency, reduce a low-frequency 'macro' blend weight in albedo) produced ZERO visible change — confirmed by pixel diff, not just eyeballing. Root-caused by bisection instead of more guessing: forced albedo, then the normal map, then roughness+AO each to a flat constant in turn. Albedo-flat alone: swirl persisted. Normal-map-flat alone: swirl persisted. Roughness+AO flat together: swirl GONE. But a first 'fix' that only narrowed roughness's existing range (still driven by the same low-frequency h) reproduced the FULL swirl at unreduced contrast — GGX specular response to roughness is highly non-linear, so shape dominates over amplitude; a small variation sharing the same macro-scale structure as h still reads as a coherent sweep. Then, with roughness/AO decoupled to high-frequency-only + flat, the swirl STILL persisted — because albedo independently reproduces it too (its own pt-driven full-strength patch mix and an h-based crack re-threshold that darkened broad low-height regions, not just actual crack lines). Real fix: rewrote albedo AND roughness/AO so neither mixes two colours at full/near-full strength across any broad, low-frequency mask — every remaining term is either high-frequency-only or a low-amplitude tint. Verified: roads-asphalt-final4.png shows genuine fine, uniform speckle with no swirl; overview and night presets re-checked for regressions, both clean. Lesson for next time: when a targeted parameter tweak produces a pixel-identical render, stop guessing and bisect by forcing whole functions to flat constants — it took four bisection rounds to find this, and every one of my first five parameter-tuning attempts (all plausible-sounding) changed nothing.

2026-09-22 fix round, first 'medium effort' item: animals update() perf. Profiled directly (temporary window.__ANIM_PROF__ instrumentation, 128 animals, 64 frames, since removed from the committed code) rather than guessing from the critic's single EMA number. Findings, honestly reported: steady-state cost is healthy (avg 0.21-0.25ms for the behaviour-step loop alone, well under the critic-checked 3ms/frame budget) — the critic's 4.18-4.997ms EMA reading is driven by intermittent spikes, not a steady overrun. Applied one real, safe fix: halved the fixed-timestep catch-up cap (beh.step() could fire up to 4 times in one frame when dt spikes past STEP=0.2s — routine under SwiftShader capture, and exactly what a real hitch on real hardware looks like too — compounding a slow frame into a worse one, the same anti-pattern zoning's own review flagged independently); halving it to 2 bounds the worst case tighter without touching simulation state (beh.step(STEP) always advances by the same fixed amount regardless of real-frame pacing, so this cannot affect determinism). Honest limitation: re-profiling after the cap change still showed an intermittent ~8ms single-call spike, roughly unchanged from before — so the catch-up multiplier was NOT the dominant cause of the worst-case number, more likely a GC pause or JS-engine hiccup coinciding with measurement in this shared, concurrently-loaded session than an O(n) cost inside beh.step() itself. Recorded as 'partially addressed, not fully explained' rather than claimed fixed — worth the critic re-measuring on a quieter machine.

2026-09-22 SELF-INFLICTED REGRESSION found by the independent critic pass and fixed same day: the 2026-09-21 waterhole-black-patch fix (terrain/water.js's in-column-scatter floor, `outgoingLight += diffuseColor.rgb * 0.45`) was a flat linear-HDR addition applied BEFORE renderer.toneMappingExposure, so it scaled with whatever exposure the scene was using. At night the exposure ceiling is 12 (vs 4 by day — see environment's own history), and the water's other light terms are already small at night, so this floor became the dominant term and blew every water body to a uniform near-white glow, brighter than the park's own lamps. The independent critic caught this in six separate contexts (terrain, animals, traffic, savannah, park module reviews, and the game's own round-5 blind pass — game.blindVisual dropped 7.8 -> 6.8 almost entirely on the strength of one shot, `game-overview-21.5`) before I had looked at a single night-time water shot after making that fix myself. Root-caused and fixed by dividing the floor by the live exposure (a new `uExposure` uniform, updated per-frame from `renderer.toneMappingExposure`) so its DISPLAY brightness stays roughly constant across day and night instead of tracking the night ceiling. Verified: night-water-fix-verify.png (game overview 21.5h) now shows dark water with a soft warm rim, lamps correctly the brightest objects in frame again; sav-waterhole-fix-recheck.png confirms the original black-patch fix still holds (dappled shade, not a hard black hole). 89/89 tests pass, lint clean. The terrain/animals/traffic/savannah/park/game scores in this file still reflect the critic's pre-fix reads and have NOT been restored by me — re-scoring is the critic's job, not mine, to keep the pass independent; flagging this fix clearly for the next critic round to re-verify rather than assuming it fully resolves those modules' scores (several also cited unrelated issues).

FOURTH AND DEEPEST ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-05: environment/atmosphere.js lightDepth() reused scatter()'s view-density scratch array _d, so every CPU-sampled sky radiance came out ~10^4x too dim (measured zenith 7e-6 vs physical ~0.5). The exposure controller, reading a near-black sky, climbed to its ceiling; the visible 'sky' was the blown-out cloud deck; fog and aerial-perspective colours near black produced the horizon band. This is the true root cause of the round-1 SYSTEMIC 'washed out toward white' blocker and of both of environment's round-2 majors — NOT ACES tone mapping, NOT albedo authoring. The GPU LUT was unaffected (GLSL locals), which is why sun colour was always right while sky/fog colours were wrong. Fixed with a separate scratch array; wave-3 verification then proceeded against a correctly-lit world.

Wave 3 (savannah, park) verified 2026-09-05: both modules were already fully implemented in the ZIP but had never been screenshotted, scored, or documented (STATUS said 'not-started' — stale). All 17 savannah presets and 7 park presets + 9 full-game sweeps shot and READ; 0 console errors everywhere; all inside the draw/triangle budgets. savannah README written; park README's two placeholder sections filled with measured numbers; missing READMEs written for environment, simulation, ui, audio; traffic's 1-line draft replaced.

Screenshot-tooling note for future rounds: park's own setSpeed(1) used to push every capture into a random night hour under SwiftShader (~35 game-hours burn during the 40-frame settle at ~1 fps) — capture pages must pass &speed=0, and modules that advance the clock must respect an explicitly paused clock. Also: do not run 3+ concurrent SwiftShader renders on a 12-core machine — module imports starve and pages time out.
Egress proxy blocks Poly Haven / ambientCG / all CDNs: every asset is procedural.
Screenshot tool renders through SwiftShader (software GL); fps in shots/*.json is NOT a GPU number. Draw calls, triangles and errors are real.

Wave 1 was interrupted mid-round by an API spend limit. Builders were killed before writing module READMEs and before their final iteration passes. Scores below are the ORCHESTRATOR's own integration review, not a full critic pass: fewer angles, no API-contract audit. Treat them as provisional and biased slightly optimistic on modules only seen at one preset.
Integration verified: all 15 modules load together in the full game with zero console errors, 278 draw calls, 4.74 M triangles (park's demo auto-builds on core:ready).

SECOND ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-04: environment/index.js clamped auto-exposure at 60x, and it was hitting 5.46x at golden hour / 60x at night on ordinary, correctly-lit scenes (Math.max(0, keyDir.y) kills the key-light term well before the sky actually looks dim as the sun nears the horizon). Every material several-fold overexposed, verified by reading a baked lion albedo texture directly (correct ~0.38 linear) against near-white on screen. Lowered the ceiling to 4 (commit e3a6999); night is now dim and legible with visible stars instead of blown to white, golden hour shows correct value separation between light/dark test objects instead of clipping everything. Needs a further tuning pass against real references but is no longer broken. This, independently of the sRGB double-encode, explains why several modules' screenshots looked washed out at low sun angles even after the sRGB fix — e.g. buildings' lodge preset (tod 17.5) flat-white background buildings.

THIRD ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-04: terrain/mesh.js had `mesh.receiveShadow = false; // BENCH`, a leftover benchmarking flag that silently blocked every shadow in the game from landing on the ground, anywhere. Fixed (commit e3a6999). This was the real cause of animals' round-1 'no contact shadow' blocker — animals had already shipped a drawn contact-shadow decal as a workaround, which stays in place as a complement now that real shadows also work.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-02: core/Textures.js gpu() double-encoded sRGB (shader-side linearToSRGBv plus an sRGB-internal-format render target). Linear 0.216 was stored as byte 188 instead of 128 — every albedo ~37% too bright. This, not ACES tone mapping, was the real cause of the project-wide washed-out look; the earlier 'author darker to compensate' guidance was a workaround over a core defect and is now WRONG. Core is fixed. Modules that compensated must have that compensation REMOVED: props is currently over-dark (near-black foliage), and any darkening added to animals/terrain/roads in round 2 must be re-checked.

issues.text: Toolbar active-tool pill renders a literal "null" as visible text (confirmed via innerHTML dump: "Building.Placenull...."). Root cause: pill.append(...) uses the native Element.append(), which stringifies a null child, instead of the project's own append() helper in dom.js which skips null/undefined. Side panel can show "0% HAPPY / Miserable" contradicted by healthy need bars (83/50/52/65/77%) and "Doing fine" advice text. The selected animal is also entirely absent from the 3D view for the same reason. Fires in the module's own panel showcase preset.

update()'s 0.5s refresh accumulator is wall-clock based, not frame-count based -- plausibly fires every frame under SwiftShader's slow frame time instead of twice a second, inflating measured updateMs (7.4-9.7ms EMA vs the 1.5ms/module budget); likely a measurement artifact of software GL rather than a confirmed real-hardware violation, but worth a frame-time-independent cap.
